name: Dubrovnik
tagline: The Pearl of the Adriatic for Mediterranean Early Retirement
description: Dubrovnik offers a fairy-tale Adriatic lifestyle with Croatia's EU membership providing straightforward residency pathways for Europeans and favorable digital nomad and passive income visa options. With stunning medieval architecture, crystal-clear waters, and costs well below Western Europe, it's an increasingly compelling FIRE destination for those seeking Mediterranean beauty without the price tag.

quickFacts.visa: Digital Nomad Visa (1 year, renewable) or Temporary Stay permit for financially independent persons. Croatia joined Schengen in 2023. EU citizens have freedom of movement.
quickFacts.internetSpeed: 50-200 Mbps fiber available in city center
quickFacts.safetyRating: Very Safe — extremely low crime, one of Europe's safest small cities
quickFacts.nearestAirport: Dubrovnik Airport (DBV) — 25 min from Old Town
quickFacts.climate: Mediterranean with mild, wet winters (8-13°C) and hot, dry summers (26-32°C). 250+ sunny days per year.

housing.description: Room in a shared flat / cheapest micro-studio, Gruž or Mokošica

dining.description: Mostly home cooking with local konobas away from the tourist strip and a daily coffee ritual

healthcare.description: Minimum compliant private/expat plan meeting the temporary-residence insurance proof

entertainment.description: Walking the city walls, swimming at Banje and the coves, kayaking to Lokrum

1M.lifestyle: A room in a shared flat or the cheapest micro-studio in Gruž or Mokošica, a short bus ride from the Old Town. Local konobas away from the tourist strip, a daily coffee ritual, and free swimming at Banje and the hidden coves make the everyday. The Libertas bus pass covers the city, and a permit-compliant private health policy is carried. Dubrovnik's tourism economy props prices higher than other Croatian towns, so the budget is workable but not loose — and the reward is the quiet off-season that visitors never see.

housing.description: Own studio/small 1BR, Gruž / Montovjerna / residential Lapad

dining.description: Good restaurants like Nautika regularly, Pelješac wine and Ston oysters

healthcare.description: Comprehensive private cover, fuller outpatient/hospital limits

entertainment.description: Dubrovnik Summer Festival seats and island-hopping to Korčula and Mljet

2M.lifestyle: A studio or small one-bedroom in residential Lapad, Montovjerna, or Gruž, some with sea glimpses. Regular dining at good restaurants like Nautika, car rentals for the Dalmatian coast, and ferry trips to Korčula and Mljet. Comprehensive private cover and front-row seats at the Dubrovnik Summer Festival fit the budget. The town is small and walkable, and the pace is relaxed.

housing.description: 1BR in a desirable central district — Ploče / Old-Town edge / upper Lapad, some sea view

dining.description: The city's best tables and private wine tours

entertainment.description: Elaphiti sailing charters, VIP festival access, scuba and golf

3M.lifestyle: A one-bedroom in a desirable central area — Ploče, the Old Town edge, or upper Lapad — often with a sea view. Regular dining at the city's best tables, a broad-network private plan with international coverage, and a car for coast road trips. Sailing through the Elaphiti islands and regular European travel are comfortably within budget. Restaurant variety is limited by the town's size, but the setting and coastal access are hard to match — and housing here already runs high for a small city because year-round rentals are genuinely scarce.

dining.description: Near-daily dining at the coast's finest restaurants

transportation.description: Car + private speedboat for island access

entertainment.description: Private yacht cruising and exclusive cultural-event hosting

5M.lifestyle: A high-spec one-bedroom in a prime spot near the Old Town or Ploče, with a sea view. Near-daily dining at the coast's best restaurants, premium private cover, regular housekeeping, and a speedboat for island access. Business-class travel and a very comfortable Adriatic life round it out. Dubrovnik's small scale means the year-round community is intimate, for better or worse.

housing.description: Luxury 1–2BR at a prime address (Old Town / Ploče), sea view — top of the thin long-term luxury pool

dining.description: Private-chef-level dining and hosted Adriatic feasts

healthcare.description: Top-tier worldwide cover (Cigna Global / Bupa Global)

transportation.description: Chauffeured car + speedboat + helicopter transfers to Split/Montenegro

entertainment.description: Cultural-festival patronage within the walls and Adriatic island retreats

domesticHelp.description: Full estate staff — limited luxury-service supply in a small walled town

luxuryExtras.description: Medieval-restoration fund, Adriatic property management, art, superyacht itineraries

10M.lifestyle: A luxury one-to-two-bedroom at a landmark address inside or beside the Old Town walls, with sea views. Private-chef-level dining, top-tier international health cover, a chauffeured car, and full household help, with a boat for Adriatic cruising. The constraint at this level is the town's intimate scale — there are limited ways to spend this much locally, so frequent travel becomes part of the lifestyle by default.
